mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior month predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce discount rates for equity valuations and stimulate economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined in the prior month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% in the prior month, it signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in private payrolls (PAYEMS) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand and corporate profit growth, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where both PAYEMS and RSAFS have increased in the prior month, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and rising), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced corporate investment.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and rising, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) over the prior month signals robust manufacturing output and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO has increased in the prior month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1200.0 thousand units in the prior month signals reduced consumer confidence and weaker economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where HOUST < 1200.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 245) and rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS increasing) signals an imminent monetary tightening cycle, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 245 and FEDFUNDS increased by at least 0.1% in prior month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 245 and FEDFUNDS increased by at least 0.1% in prior month, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong supply expansion (INDPRO > 105 and rising), the S&P 500 experiences positive returns over the next 5 trading days due to increased corporate output and profit margins.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO > 105 and rising, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
